name: onboarding
title: Onboarding
description: The sequence a player is walked through before they play: an illustration, a step, the pager saying where in the sequence this is, and a way forward with a way out beside it. The step is a real `tutorial-step` and the pager is `segments` in its pager treatment, the same row of cells the round indicator and a quest's progress use, so neither is written again here and both keep their own root marker; a one-step sequence draws no pager at all. The way forward is the library's `button`, so a theme's button roles reach it. The pager is derived from the step rather than passed, so the two cannot disagree. Position is `data-gs-step` over `data-gs-max`, the same pair progress uses. A finished sequence carries `data-gs-complete`; a skipped one carries `data-gs-dismissed` and renders nothing inside, because leaving controls in an aria-hidden subtree is a keyboard trap for the player that rule exists for. Performs nothing: it does not advance itself, remember the player has seen it, or decide the sequence is done.
docs: Pass `steps`, one entry per step with a `title`, a `body` and an optional `media` slot for the illustration or animation, and `step` for the one the sequence is on, from 1. Pass `onNext`, `onBack` and `onDismiss` to get the three controls; a sequence with none renders no controls at all, because the component never invents a way forward the host did not ask for. Pass `heading` for the small heading that names the game or the show, and `titlePlacement="above"` to draw it with the title over the card rather than in it, as a broadcaster's how-to-play does (GSUI-375). A one-step sequence draws no pager, because one cell saying you are here is not a position (GSUI-376). Pass `complete` when the host says the sequence is done and `dismissed` when the player closed it; neither is inferred from the step number. A step out of range renders nothing rather than throwing, and the attributes still carry what the host asked for. It imports `./tutorial-step`, `./segments` and `./button`, which are the flat paths a `gamestage-ui add` produces, and `@gamestage/tutorial-step`, `@gamestage/segments` and `@gamestage/button` are what put those files there.
